subject: Rapid recap: decision rubric & next tests
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Kaur <priya.kaur@datapulse.com>, Alex Mercer <alex@cloudhealth.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Rapid recap: decision rubric & next tests

Thanks for the call today — quick written recap so we have a shared checklist and owners. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary (what we heard)
- Primary pain: unpredictable inference cost at peak traffic and long tail latency spikes during concurrent batch jobs.
- Secondary: ops visibility gaps (per-route token-level cost) and the need for deterministic rollbacks in case of an output-quality regression.
- Success criteria: P95 latency <= 350ms at 1k rps sustained for 10m; per-route cost below $0.003/token (weekly aggregated).

Decision rubric (shared basis)
- Latency profile (P50/P95) under typical and stressed workload — weighting 35%
- Unit economics at scale (batching + quantization) — weighting 25%
- Security & auditability (KMS, audit logs) — weighting 15%
- Operational UX (rollouts, tracing, per-token cost) — weighting 15%
- Integrations & support (VPC options, marketplace onboarding) — weighting 10%

Agreed open tests and owners
1) Latency soak: Redwood to run a 30-minute P95 soak at 1k rps with 2x concurrent KV-cache-heavy requests. Deliverable: latency + tail breakdown, kernel choices, and config used. (Owner: Logan / Camila)
2) Cost delta: Redwood to produce a simulated monthly cost at expected traffic with and without prefix caching and two quantization profiles. Deliverable: cost model spreadsheet. (Owner: Aditya)
3) Security evidence: share SOC2 scope summary + sample audit log export (anonymized). (Owner: Marissa)
4) Parity probe: short prompt-based end-to-end parity checks vs. other vendors for the top-10 intents. Deliverable: prompt set + output diff and quality notes. (Owner: DataPulse / Priya to provide baseline intents)

Attachments: redwood-poc-asks.pdf (POC steps & test endpoints), decision-rubric-v1.xlsx (blank rubric to score vendors)

Timing
- Redwood to deliver latency soak results and cost model by 2026-09-10 EOD PT.
- Schedule POC run week of 9/13 if results look aligned.

Next steps (quick list)
- Priya: confirm top-10 intents and provide sample traffic shape (p95/p99 load bursts).
- Alex: share any vendor-specific tests you want included for parity.
- Logan/Camila/Aditya/Marissa: execute the three deliverables and send results to this thread.

Thanks — appreciate the crisp call.

—
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Logan — this matches our notes. A couple clarifications from DataPulse side: 
- Top-10 intents: I'll send CSV of intents + a single canonical prompt example by EOD. We have a mix of short transactional and long-context follow-ups; please treat both.
- For parity probes: please include failure-type tags (hallucination, truncation, format mismatch) so we can score quality consistently.

Also: we have a procurement gating item — need a short note on data residency options (multi-region availability) for our security team. If you can include that with the SOC2 evidence it helps speed review.

Agree on 9/10 for the initial deliverables.

Best,
Priya
Head of Product, DataPulse

Good notes. Two quick requests from CloudHealth AI's side that we think are important to surface in the bakeoff: 
1) Cold-start behavior: show cold vs warm P90/P95 after a model file swap and after cache eviction. That's been a real pain in our infra.
2) Tokenization parity: include token counts and normalized cost per semantic unit for comparison — different tokenizers skew unit economics.

If Redwood can provide a short technical note on KV cache eviction policy (how long KV entries persist, TTL behavior across restarts) that'll be very helpful for our engineers.

Finally — scheduling: I'm available for a 30m follow-up on Thu 9/9 (afternoon PT). If Logan wants to lock that in, put it in the calendar.

—
Alex Mercer
